claims.value: In 1815, Upper Canada and Lower Canada remained separate colonial provinces under the 1791 constitutional arrangements. Each had its own appointed councils and elected assembly. Their union into the Province of Canada belonged to a later constitutional phase; the federal Dominion established in 1867 is not projected backward.

sources.usage: Read historical body and chronology, especially 1791 separate Upper/Lower Canada, maritime colonies, 1867 union effective 1 July, and 1934 Newfoundland suspension. The broad chronology oversimplifies Newfoundland’s 1931 statute applicability; original section 10 controls instead. Modern officeholder rules and representation counts excluded.
